summary.headline: Amber signs Oppo manufacturing collaboration for mobile phones, targeting ~8 million units in year 1 of commercial production (FY28), with minimal capex below INR50 crore initially.
summary.overview: Amber Enterprises held a business update call on 20 June 2026 to discuss a manufacturing collaboration agreement with Oppo Mobiles India, executed 18 June 2026, covering Oppo, OnePlus and Realme brands. The company frames this as its entry into mobile phone manufacturing, starting with assembly and SMT, and as a diversification away from seasonal room air conditioner demand. Trial production is slated for Q4 FY27 and commercial production for Q1 FY28, with volumes ramping from ~8 million units to 13-15 million units in the second year. Management gave limited financial detail: the commercial model (gross vs job work) is undecided, margins are described as industry-like, and the reporting segment and entity structure are still to be decided.

segments.name: Mobile phone manufacturing (Oppo/OnePlus/Realme)
segments.commentary: Assembly and SMT first, with HDI PCBs planned from year 2; manufacturing to be done at an existing Oppo facility under a sublease with exclusivity. Commercial terms (sale-purchase vs job work) depend on Oppo India, so revenue recognition could be gross on some models and net on others.

segments.name: PCB (Ascent / Shogini)
segments.commentary: Amber now holds 98.5% of Ascent, up from 60%. Management said the PCB division will be headed by Mr. Santosh, who has about 25 years of experience and previously headed AT&S. Management said Amber is now the largest PCB company with Ascent and Shogini.

guidance_outlook: Trial production to start in Q4 FY27; commercial production from Q1 FY28, with a learning curve of about the first 3 months.
Year 1 of commercial production around 8 million units (8-9 million), with conservative planning at 8 million; 13-15 million units expected in year 2 or by FY29-FY30.
Targeting local value addition of 30%-40% over the next 5-6 years, versus about 10-12% for the industry today.
Component additions (camera modules, displays, metal casings, and others) to follow once volumes reach 14-15 million, with the roadmap still to be formalised.
Management said it would go slow and add other brands (such as Vivo) only after reaching the Oppo volume targets.
capex_capacity: Initial capex for assembly and SMT is below INR50 crore, with no major capex at the start, since the facility is subleased from Oppo India.
Component capex will come after volumes reach 14-15 million units; management said there will be no duplication with existing PCB capex.
Existing capability at IL JIN: 9-10 million smart watches per year, close to 15 million PCB assemblies per year, and more than 5.5 million AC boxes per year.
Management said the Oppo sublease covers a dedicated, exclusive production line at a large compound.
The business may sit under Amber or IL JIN; the decision is pending and will be communicated before operations start.
demand_pricing: India's mobile phone market is flat in volume, but rising ASPs are driving replacement demand toward high-end phones, per management.
Industry local value addition is about 10-12%; most players do assembly only, and a few do assembly plus SMT.

Management said the business is low-margin, high-volume, similar to its smart watch business, with industry EBITDA of 1.5%-2% excluding PLI. The arrangement is on bottom-line economics, with flexibility on top-line recognition.
Management said the company is not disturbing Oppo's existing EMS ecosystem, and Oppo has been asked not to give other business to competitors.
Management said Vivo has no arrangement at present. A second PLI framework is still at the speculation stage, with no draft yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will Amber recognise revenue gross (ODM-style) or only on value addition, and how does it build expertise?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue treatment depends on Oppo India's commercial model, with some models gross and some net; bottom-line economics are intact. Expertise comes from group scale (smart watches, PCBs, ACs), and the first 3 months are a learning curve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI and backward integration plan, and will other BBK brands or Vivo be added?
qa_highlights.answer: The second PLI draft is not available, so no comment on structure. The arrangement covers Oppo, OnePlus and Realme. There is no Vivo arrangement; Amber will add brands only after reaching the 14-15 million target.

qa_highlights.question: Is the business likely to be scalable beyond Oppo given a flat phone market?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will come from local value addition, moving from 10-12% to 35-40% over 5-6 years, adding HDI in year 2 and further components later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity of the leased facility and how does it fit with Oppo's other EMS partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Oppo has a large compound with dedicated lines that can be subleased exclusively; Amber is targeting 20-30% of Oppo's volume without disturbing its existing ecosystem.

qa_highlights.question: What are the working capital needs, ROCE, and capex for the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 4-5 days, maximum 10 days. Standalone ROCE is expected above 30-35%. Initial capex is below INR50 crore, with component capex later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the business be housed in Amber or IL JIN, and who will lead it?
qa_highlights.answer: The structure is undecided and will be announced before operations start, with IL JIN a likely home given wearables and other shareholders. A dedicated senior management team will be set up.

risks_watch: No revenue, EBITDA or contract value disclosed; commercial model (gross vs job work) and segment reporting are still undecided.
Margins are low (industry EBITDA 1.5%-2% ex-PLI), so the financial contribution depends on volume ramp.
Execution risk: trial production in Q4 FY27 and commercial production in Q1 FY28 must hold, and the year 2 volume target of 13-15 million is conditional ('if everything goes as scheduled').
Management said the second PLI structure is unknown; any value-add linked incentive is a potential upside but not yet defined.
Ascent PCB leadership changed (MD Mr. Manjunath stepped down after the stake rise to 98.5%); the new head is Mr. Santosh.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on strategic fit and long-term value addition, but noticeably vague on commercial and financial specifics, deferring the revenue model, entity structure and PLI details to Oppo and later announcements.
key_quotes: This collaboration meaningfully diversifies our revenue profile and importantly, reduces the seasonal concentration inherent in our room air conditioner business.
To start with on the assembly and SMT, we are not putting in any capex. It will be minimum. It will be below INR50 crores to start with.
So, the arrangement is on the bottom line side, not on the top line side basically. We have a flexibility on the top line side.
Generally, these are very ROCE accretive. If you take this on a stand-alone basis, I mean, the ROCEs will be more than 30%, 35%.
